title: Embedding evaluation orchestrator: nightly reference sets, synthetic perturbations, and drift signalization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a single orchestrated harness that runs deterministic offline evaluations for embedding quality across model variants, generates synthetic perturbations to test robustness, and derives drift signals for automatic alerting. Current ad-hoc scripts live in multiple repos and only cover MRR or pairwise similarity; they miss label stratification, latency-aware buckets, and end-to-end pipeline reliability.

Goal: Build an Embedding Evaluation Orchestrator (EEO) that: 1) runs nightly canonical reference set evaluations (seeded, reproducible), 2) synthesizes perturbation families (typos, paraphrase, truncation, domain shift) and measures sensitivity, 3) emits per-model/per-route offline metrics (MRR@1/3, p@1, NDCG, mean cosine, embedding drift score) and latency-aware quality breakdowns, and 4) surfaces drift/quality alerts to Console and Slack with suggested mitigations (roll back to variant, reduce batch size, mark model for re-eval).

Non-goal: This ticket does not include UI work in Console; it focuses on the backend harness, telemetry export, and alert ruleset. Console wiring will be a separate PM/design ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly pipeline runs on schedule (UTC 03:00) and stores results in eval-store with stable keys (model:version:date)
At least three synthetic perturbation families implemented and pluggable (typo, paraphrase, truncation)
Per-model CSV/JSON output contains MRR@1/3, p@1, mean cosine, sample coverage, and p95 latency buckets
Drift score computed daily (cosine shift + distribution KL on sector buckets) and an alerting rule created for > 3 sigma change
Pipeline includes stratified sampling by customer traffic segment and a reproducible seed for golden queries
Playbook added: when alert fires include candidate mitigations and the rollback model version ID
tasks: Design canonical reference set schema and serializer (compact + human-readable)
Implement perturbation library with deterministic seeds and configurable magnitudes
Build orchestrator job (K8s CronJob -> Airflow DAG prototype) that runs per-region and aggregates outputs
Add telemetry exporters for metrics (Prometheus + metric labels) and write eval artifacts to eval-store (S3 path)
Create alert rule in PagerDuty/Slack via existing infra (alert if drift_score > threshold AND sample_count > 100)
Write unit + integration tests and a local dev runner for reproducibility
Document runbook and add example queries + golden set curation notes
comments: 2026-02-13 | Marco Li: Initial architecture sketch posted in #embeddings. Prefers Airflow DAG to K8s CronJob for retries and lineage. Will prototype with a single-region job first.
2026-02-20 | Asha Patel: Added canonical-reference schema draft to Confluence (link below). Decided to include metadata fields: origin, label, domain, traffic_segment.
2026-02-28 | R&D (Samantha Ortiz): Ran synthetic paraphrase sensitivity tests on a sample model; paraphrases drop MRR by 8% for small models. Suggest adding a paraphrase severity knob.
2026-03-03 | Infra (Devon Chen): Storage plan: eval artifacts to s3://redwood-evals/{env}/{model}/{date}/manifest.json. Recommend compressing older artifacts with zstd to save cost.
2026-03-05 | Marcos (PM): Request to include latency buckets (p50/p90/p95) in the output since customers correlate quality regressions with tail latency spikes. Added as AC.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Prototype runs nightly for dev/staging models and generates artifacts (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Run for 5 production models with read-only alerts (no PagerDuty) to gather baseline (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Enable alerting for high-risk models and integrate with Console and PagerDuty (1 week)
Phase 4: Expand to all production model routes and add automated mitigation playbooks (ongoing)
decisions: Use stratified sampling by traffic_segment to ensure small-customer queries are represented
Compute drift as weighted cosine centroid shift + KL on binned norms to capture both mean shift and distributional change
Synthetic perturbations must be deterministic (seeded) to allow regression attribution
Store full artifact in S3 and export summarized metrics to Prometheus + Timeseries DB for long-term trends
tradeoffs: Compute cost vs coverage: running many perturbation magnitudes increases signal but costs more GPU/CPU time
Alert sensitivity: tighter thresholds reduce missed regressions but increase false positives — will iterate based on baseline false-positive rate
Storage retention: keeping full artifacts for 1 year is useful for audits but expensive; propose tiered retention (90d hot, 1y cold)
